title: Case Study: Why Copilot Stays in Search Mode

title: Senior Engineers Still Use Copilot Like Advanced Search
keyMessage: The default state of Copilot adoption is search mode.
quotes: Most of the org treats Copilot like an advanced Google search.
bottomLine: Copilot stays in Q&A mode when work has no durable system for Copilot to operate against.

title: Knowing the Mechanics != Running Work Through Copilot
keyMessage: Training can teach what Copilot can do, but it does not automatically change how engineering work is executed.
quotes: The average one does not understand agents or skills.
bottomLine: Feature awareness is not workflow transformation.

title: How Copilot Adoption Actually Evolves
bullets: Exploration: prompt-based usage, Q&A, code help
Friction: no durable workflow, context, or structure
System Installation: specs, decisions, repo, templates, instructions
Workflow Integration: Copilot embedded in daily execution
Scale: pattern reused across teams and projects

title: Externalize -> Structure -> Install -> Execute -> Repeat
bullets: Externalize: bring real artifacts, decisions, and constraints into view
Structure: turn scattered thinking into design and boundaries
Install: create a system Copilot can work against
Execute: use Copilot inside the system
Repeat: scale the pattern across projects

bullets: From Demo to Real Design templates
bottomLine: Motion: initial ask -> enablement -> real design -> system installation -> Copilot-led execution -> repeat.

title: The Lesson from Honeywell
keyMessage: Copilot remains advanced search until the work is externalized into a system it can operate against.
